rationale: M60 groovy lane (2026-09-25). The override pass reaches a method's parent through `classHierarchy`, keyed by the OWNER's FQN. handleObjectCreationExpression built an anonymous type's symbol, registered its symbolMap key and pushed its scope (with `parents: [superName]`) — but never wrote the hierarchy entry, so every override TASK inside an anonymous body found no parents at any of the three tiers and emitted nothing at all. Measured at full extent on the 4,014-file grails-core draw: the lane's only MISSING rows were `overrides anonymous_IdentityTypeDecoder.bsonType -> IdentityTypeDecoder.bsonType` (IdentityDecoder.groovy) and `overrides anonymous_TypeDecoder.bsonType -> TypeDecoder.bsonType` (SimpleDecoder.groovy). Note the differential's coverage match is LEAF-based (normTarget = lastSegment), so the sibling `anonymous_X.decode -> X.decode` truth rows were masked by a leaf collision with the analyzer's own superclass-resolution edge `IdentityDecoder.decode -> PropertyDecoder.decode` — the corpus count under-reported the defect by half, and this fixture pins the TARGET as well as the leaf so a leaf collision can never hide it again. The `Registry.bsonType -> BaseCodec.bsonType` row is the control: the ordinary named-subclass override must be untouched, and it is the shape a fix that repaired the anonymous case by breaking the named one would visibly move.

Vacuous today (the anon scope owns the method), and pinned for the day the attribution moves — that shape is what the pre-fix silence would become if the missing hierarchy entry were 'fixed' by widening the owner to the enclosing type instead.
